name: Flashlight grip for sliding bike handlebar mounts

captions.detailed: This 3D-printable part is a customized flashlight mount designed to fit onto a sliding bike rail. It consists of a large main hollow cylinder with a longitudinal gap on one side, flanked by two rectangular clamping flanges containing three bolt holes each with hexagonal nut recesses. On the opposite side of the cylinder, there is a flat sliding mount adapter featuring a T-shaped slot profile and a small rectangular spring-clip hole near the top.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric bike flashlight mount in OpenSCAD that features a cylindrical clamp, clamping flanges with adjustable bolt and hexagonal nut holes, and a sliding rail adapter. The user should be able to customize parameters such as the inner and outer cylinder radii, the bolt and nut sizes, the clamping gap width, and the sliding rail dimensions.
captions.factory: The model is constructed using four main modules: grip(), flange(), flanges(), and slide(). The grip() module creates the main hollow cylinder using a difference of two cylinder primitives, with a cube subtracting a longitudinal gap. The flanges() module places two rectangular flange cubes, subtracting bolt holes (cylinders rotated 90 degrees) on one side and hexagonal nut recesses (six-sided cylinders) on the other. The slide() module builds the rail adapter by subtracting two nested rectangular channels from a main block, and a small rectangular hole is subtracted from the final assembly using a cube.
